newsitem.title: CUBA: U.S. authorities return three Cuban rafters.
newsitem.headline: U.S. authorities return three Cuban rafters.

text.p: The U.S. Coast Guard returned three Cuban rafters on Friday, bringing to 612 the number of Cubans sent home in the last two years after being intercepted trying illegally to reach the United States, state media said.
The state news agency AIN said the three set off a week ago from the eastern province of Camaguey, were intercepted by the U.S. Coast Guard and were returned to Cabanas.

Cabanas is a small port west of Havana that has been used for repatriations by the U.S. Coast Guard since a landmark May 1995 Cuba-U.S. accord on immigration that aimed to halt the flow of Cuban boat people towards Florida.
Under the agreement Washington undertook to return Cubans that U.S. authorities intercepted trying to reach the United States by illegal means.
Of the total 612 people sent back to Cuba, most were intercepted in the Florida Strait, but 146 were caught trying to cross to the U.S. Naval Base at Guantanamo Bay on the southeast tip of Cuba.
The May 1995 accord followed a September 1994 bilateral agreement that sought to stem an exodus of more than 30,000 Cuban rafters in August and September 1994.
